utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that there was one stupid thing more said relating to the events over there. I remember well that he described that he was passing through the hangar by chance. He was going to get a part for a car or some machine, and then in passing he saw that people were fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he say that he himself had done something that was not permitted in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: He said something that is well-known, but he did not say the real truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How do you know that that was not the real truth?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because Mr. Livingston, in his investigation, came out with such facts which indicate for certain that that man is lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you have that information?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you can ask that of Mr. Livingston.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, did you sign a letter sent to Mrs. Bilana Plavsic, which was published in Novasti dated May 14th, 1998, as one of the seven detainees in The Hague, and you were the first, number one on the list? This is document 507.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: All right. Did you send a letter to Mr. Vujin dated March 5th, 1998? That's Exhibit number 507. Can you tell us something about that letter?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as the letter to Mrs. Plavsic is concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No. No, I just asked you whether you had signed that letter. Now we're moving on to this other letter.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, if you permit me, I would like to say something about this other letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Well, there's no need. I just mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, may I ask if this is an exhibit? If I'm not allowed to refer to it, to say anything about it, I would ask the Court's permission to state something because the information presented by Mr. Vujin's Defence is incorrect regarding this letter. I received the information about this before, and I believe that I can comment on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, I think we shall make progress if you attended to the questions asked of you by learned counsel and limit your answers to the questions which he asks.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I say something on that very briefly? I quite appreciate that obviously in cross-examination one is asked questions and one makes answers to those questions. In this case, of course, I don't have a right of re-examination. He has been referred to a document merely to ask "Did you sign it, yes or no," and then swiftly the question moved on. I don't anticipate that his answer is going to be very long, but otherwise the matter is left in the air and will never be cleared up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Abell. What is clear to the Tribunal is his answer whether he signed or didn't sign the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: My next question was about Mr. Tadic's letter to Mr. Vujin dated March 5th, 1998, and that's number 257 in the documents. Could the witness say whether he sent this letter and the reasons for sending it?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have that letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, could you explain why you wrote that letter at that time and why you sent it to Mr. Vujin?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: This letter was accompanied by a series of documents, as you can see, "from sources." That source was Mr. Delalic who was on trial for the Celebici case, and he asked me to send this to the counsel because he felt that this was important.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the Celebici case.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you get some information connected with that which you sent to Mr. Vujin in order to prove that there was no international armed conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is what was of interest to Mr. Vujin above everything else, and he thought that I should send that. Mr. Delalic gave that to me and I sent that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you know that the responsibility of the accused in the proceedings depended on the nature, on the definition of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't sure whether this was relevant to my case. It was relevant, in my estimate, to the responsible persons that were awaiting trial in front of this Court or could be accused and also for the proceedings against Yugoslavia initiated by Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, did you give instructions to Mr. Vujin on what circumstances he was to question witnesses Bozan Grahovac, Zigic, Stoja Coprka, Milos Preradovic, Vlado Krckovski, and some others?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: What kind of instructions do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What circumstances the witnesses would be questioned about.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I expressed my opinion regarding the information that I received from other attorneys or members of my family who had found something out regarding these people, so that I just basically expressed what I had found out which could be used in the questioning of these people. I could not directly influence the questions that he would put to these persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could the witness look at document 266 and tell us whether this was a document in question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is this your instruction?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think this is incomplete, since it starts from number 30 and ends at number 32. It is my handwriting, however, but this is not any kind of instruction. I just said it was just information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall the instructions that you gave Mr. Vujin before the Court when there was a conflict between you and Mr. Wladimiroff and you ended your cooperation with Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this was not any kind of conflict, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you look at document 551 and if you would kindly read it?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have the English version in front of me. I don't know ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please read it? It's very brief, if I remember right.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Vujin needed a reason to explain in public why he had become part of the team again, and he told me to write down this text and then I wrote this: "... emphasised that between me and Wladimiroff there has been a conflict because he didn't want to defend me on count 1," and this was told to me only after the trial. So a few days after the verdict, we cut off our cooperation, and I think Mr. Vujin needed a public reason to explain why he joined the Defence again, but this was not the true reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you ask Mr. Vujin to interview Mr. Kos as a witness, and who was supposed to conduct this interview?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think that I asked that, taught by my experience regarding the questioning of Mr. Radic and Mr. Kvocka, where I expected Mr. Vujin to take expanded statements from these people on April 18th regarding really important things because these people were holding important posts. I don't think that I asked him to take a statement from Kos. I think that I asked that exclusively Mr. Livingston do this, and Vujin had to respect the full procedure to get the consent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did Mr. Vujin do this?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did Mr. Livingston question or interview the witness?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. He arrived at The Hague, but the witness and his counsel refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honours, my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In the statement of November 24th, Mr. Tadic, you say that there had been a conflict between you and Mr. Vujin because of submissions about whose contents you had not been informed and that, as you state here, you urged Mr. Vujin in a letter to respect the basic codes of behaviour and that Mr. Vujin angrily and threateningly responded that he was going to leave your case.

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this refer to the response of Mr. Vujin to the Prosecution's appeal?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: The worst thing was that I was not sure what kind of a submission this was about. I got information from representatives of the Registry who were surprised why this submission was tendered before the deadline. Mr. Vujin found out about this by accident, and he asked me why this was submitted. I didn't know why this was submitted, and I asked Mr. Vujin to withdraw this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did Mr. Vujin agree to withdraw the submission?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he respond that he did not want to withdraw one single word and that if you were not satisfied, you could withdraw your power of attorney?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes, there was such an answer, and it was very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Why did you not at that time withdraw your power of attorney from Mr. Vujin?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that was ridiculous for me to change attorneys in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So in that period after the appeal, why did you think that was ridiculous?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because it was a kind of blackmail. It was presented as a kind of blackmail. I was supposed to be left hanging in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But after that, you did withdraw the power of attorney?

utterances.speaker: Dusko Tadic (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, once I had ascertained the correctness of the information that I had been receiving for years, that Mr. Vujin had been tampering with witnesses, especially (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, if you had not told us differently, we would not have had any reason to believe that you had had no previous exposure to the adversarial system. Professionally, I would like to congratulate you. Are there any questions? Yes. The witness is excused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The witness is an interested party, Mr. Abell --

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: -- and the officers of the Court will make arrangements for the witness to be accommodated within this room. Was that your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: That was precisely my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: He's an interested party.
